request.spec:
A button downloads the people of the whole tree as a CSV file: a header line
sheet,name,grade,due-total then one line per person, this sheet first in list order, then the
other sheets of the tree by sheet id.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the people of the whole tree as a CSV file: a header line
sheet,name,grade,due-total then one line per person, this sheet first in list order, then the
other sheets of the tree by sheet id.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added an "Export tree CSV" button that downloads everyone in the sheet's whole tree, and all 4 acceptance tests pass when I run `bin/e2e`.

The file starts with the header `sheet,name,grade,due-total`. Then come this sheet's people in list order, then the other sheets in the tree, sorted by sheet id. Each person's grade is the one in force on their own sheet's "today". Their due-total is the one their sheet shows, or `n/a` if there isn't one.

**Server:** a new `TreeExportController.java` in the `rollup` package answers `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/tree-export`. It uses the same rules as the existing tree search to find the tree, order the sheets and work out the figures, so the two always agree.

**Front end:** the `export-tree` button is in the "Search the tree" section (`tree-search.ts`). It builds the file with the app's existing CSV helper. If the request fails, it shows an error with the `data-testid` `export-tree-error`. That id isn't in the test, so I chose the name.

- **No audit record:** the export changes nothing, so it writes nothing to the audit file.
- **Ignores the as-of date:** it always shows current figures, even while an as-of date is set. This differs from the people export on the same screen, which re-reads the as-of figures. The test doesn't check this either way.

The new controller repeats about a dozen lines from the tree search controller rather than sharing them. They could be moved into one shared method if you want.
